title: Province's police watchdog offers more detail in fatal Saskatoon police shooting
article: The agency responsible for investigating the actions of Saskatchewan police officers has offered a few more details of what allegedly occurred when Saskatoon officers last week shot and killed a man.

City police reported in a June 20 media release that officers responding to a gun call had opened fire on a 27-year-old suspect, killing him. They further announced that the Serious Incident Response Team (SIRT) would investigate the actions of the officers involved.
A SIRT media release issued on Monday provided a brief timeline of events leading up to and immediately after the fatal shooting.
Police were called around 10:35 a.m. with a report that a man had fired a single shot from a shotgun in the area of 20th Street West and Avenue U South, the SIRT media release said.
The caller gave police a description of a suspect and a group of people he was allegedly travelling with, then stayed on the phone with police while providing updates on the group's location.

The caller ended the call just before 10:45 a.m., the SIRT release said. About one minute later, two members of the city police tactical support unit came upon a group resembling the description provided by the caller near 20th Street West and Avenue S South.

The suspect and the officers then got into what the media release described as "a confrontation," during which two officers fired their pistols, hitting the man. Paramedics arrived around 10:50 a.m. and pronounced him dead at the scene a short time later.
City police notified SIRT of the incident shortly after it occurred and a SIRT team was sent to begin an investigation into the police actions during the incident leading to the man's death.
The SIRT investigators recovered ammunition and "items believed to be components of a firearm" from the scene, which have been secured for further testing, the SIRT release said.

While SIRT will investigate the city police officers' handling of the incident, city police will maintain authority over any further investigation into the original call received prior to the suspect's death.

SIRT was established by provincial legislation passed in 2021, and came into service in 2023. It's a civilian-led, independent organization with a mandate to investigate actions or omissions of on- and off-duty police officers in cases of serious injury or death, sexual assault or interpersonal violence.
